title: Editorial: Rays of hope
gist: Prospect's editorial argues right-wing populism is being pushed back globally in late 2026: Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil, Vučić conceded to Serbia's Student List, Republicans lost both chambers in the US midterms and Netanyahu's bloc lost 15 seats, with the cost of living (inflation fuelled by the Ukraine and Iran conflicts) the unifying driver and Trump's peak power now passed.

insights.claim: Brazil's incumbent Lula defeated far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, who has disputed the result but is not in power; Lula, 81, begins a fourth term.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Continuity of a left-leaning Brazilian government; watch for post-election dispute noise but limited institutional risk.

insights.claim: In Serbia, veteran leader Aleksandar Vučić admitted defeat to the Student List, a party born of a mass student-led protest movement, after a snap parliamentary election.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Regime change in Serbia could shift its EU/Russia balancing; reassess Balkan political risk.

insights.claim: Donald Trump's Republican party lost control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate in the 2026 midterms.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Divided government constrains Trump's legislative agenda for the rest of his term; legislative gridlock and oversight risk rise.

insights.claim: Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost by a massive 15 seats to the opposition in Israel, and his attempts to question the results have so far fallen on deaf ears.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Potential change in Israeli government stance relevant to Iran conflict and regional risk premia.
insights.quote: Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc went down by a massive 15 seats

insights.claim: In the UK under Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Nigel Farage's Reform is joint-fourth by share of seats.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.quote: Nigel Farage’s Reform is joint-fourth in terms of its share of seats

themes.theme: Cost of living as the decisive political fact

insights.claim: The editorial argues the common thread across these elections, and across student protests in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Belgium, Austria and Greece, is a lack of hope that living standards will improve.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Real-income stagnation is driving anti-incumbent and anti-populist swings alike; economic underperformance is the key political risk variable.

insights.claim: The conflicts in Ukraine and Iran have fuelled inflation and squeezed household budgets globally, making the cost of living the most salient political fact of the times.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: War-driven inflation keeps the cost of living at the centre of politics; energy-price shocks translate directly into electoral outcomes.
insights.quote: the cost of living remains the most salient political fact of the times

insights.claim: Prospect sees a solution to weak growth and cost-of-living pressure as a distant prospect in many nations, especially in the European Union.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Implies prolonged EU stagnation and continued political volatility in the bloc.

insights.claim: The editorial attributes the Republicans' midterm thrashing to Trump deploying armed personnel to arrest citizens, apparent self-enrichment, a needless war that inflated prices on top of tariffs, and targeting close democratic allies.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Tariffs plus war-driven inflation proved electorally toxic; expect pressure on Trump to moderate trade and war policy.

insights.claim: Prospect judges that the high point of Trump's power has passed, though a volatile Trump with time running down may remain a dangerous presence in the world.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Lame-duck dynamics may raise foreign-policy volatility even as domestic power shrinks.
insights.quote: But the high point of Trump’s power has passed.

insights.claim: US courts countrywide have resisted the Trump administration's attempts at manipulation, indicating liberal-democratic institutions are seriously damaged but not destroyed.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Institutional resilience lowers tail risk of US constitutional breakdown.
insights.locator: It is always important for liberals

insights.claim: The editorial cautions against running these results together: Lula heads a near half-century-old party, Serbia saw new entrants, and US politics is more exception than rule.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Avoid extrapolating a single global 'anti-populist' trade; each case is local.
